issue.title: Unblock E2 (sase-1n6): green exercise legs, a current steward verdict, a published core pin, and an executing handover gate
issue.description: sase-1n6.10 can watch and prove the first steward release. A master rehearsal of release.yml is green end to end, including both wheel exercise legs. Master pins a complete published sase-core-rs whose tag contains its source revision. A failed core cut that a newer green cut superseded no longer stops the steward. One human approval turns on merge authority, leaves the pypi environment tag-only, and relaunches sase-1n6.10 with corrected instructions.

CORRECTED WAIT PROCEDURE: Poll `python3 tools/ratchet_core_pin --check --fetch --ref origin/master` every 300s with about a 36h deadline, and exit on 0 or 2. Polling the working tree waits on a frozen pin, which is why note #4's continuation found master had moved. Continuation: on exit, run the same command again at once, and dispatch the rehearsal in the same turn if it still exits 0 or 2. Exit 2 keeps its existing core_version override rule (`-f core_version=<core-ensure pick>`). If the race is lost again, start a new poll with the same command. Never poll a workspace checkout. Step 5 (release-PR sync) gets the same fallback as step 4: if the release PR's pinned core cannot match the rehearsal within about 48h, raise the gate anyway, and name the mismatch and its owner (the steward, after the handover) in the gate notes, so the phase never stalls silently. The release PR is now #322 ("release 0.19.0").

real-cuts (sase-1pi.2): what the handover gate notes must now state. Under cut_budget=daily, turning merge authority on also lets the steward dispatch up to one core cut per UTC day: a CORE_LAG tick proposes dispatch_core_cut only when no workflow_dispatch cut started earlier the same UTC day, otherwise it reports the lag suppressed for the day. Push and six-hourly heal runs are not cuts, so a green push at the lagging pin no longer reads as already_satisfied. Live 2026-10-29: pin 65546fd2 lags newest_complete 0.43.0; tick reports core_ci_red until macos-core lands.
